Package net.sourceforge.plantuml.teavm.js.browser

Class PendingResources

java.lang.Object
net.sourceforge.plantuml.teavm.js.browser.PendingResources
public final class PendingResources extends Object
The resources a rendering needs from the JavaScript side, which only arrive asynchronously: support scripts (emoji.js, themes.js, <lib>.min.js...), files of the host's PLANTUML_FILE_LOADER, and the Viz.js instance.

Why

The Java code of PlantUML is synchronous: an !include reads its file and goes on. Waiting for JavaScript in the middle of it would need TeaVM's coroutines (threads, Object.wait(), @Async), which turn every method above the waiting point into a state machine. The engine uses none of them. Instead, a rendering is an attempt that can be thrown away:
  1. A loader that does not have its resource yet does not wait: it notes it here as missing, and fails as it fails when the resource does not exist.
  2. At the end of the attempt, RenderQueue looks at the missing resources. None: the result is delivered. Otherwise the attempt is discarded, everything missing is loaded with plain JavaScript callbacks (loadMissing(ScriptLoaderJs.Ok)), and the rendering starts again from the beginning.
Each round discovers the next level: the includes of an included file, a theme chosen by a variable, the bundle a stdlib library links to. Parsing and rendering rebuild everything from the source lines, so a discarded attempt leaves nothing behind but what is kept here.

What is kept, and for how long

What the loaders answered, success or failure, is kept for the current request only (startRequest()): the next request asks the host again, so an edited file or a fixed network is seen at the next rendering. A failure is kept too, so that a resource that cannot be loaded is not loaded again at every round. Loaded scripts are global to the page anyway, and so is the Viz.js instance.

A host that never answers does not leave the engine waiting forever: after ROUND_TIMEOUT_MS the resources still pending count as failed, with a message saying so, and the rendering goes on (a late answer is ignored). Nothing blocks meanwhile: the timer is a JavaScript one.

Outside an attempt (the synchronous exports of the headless build, such as checkSyntax) nothing is noted: a resource that is not there yet simply fails.

    • MAX_ROUNDS

      public static final int MAX_ROUNDS
      How many times a request may be rendered again because resources were missing. Each round loads every resource the attempt asked for, so this is a depth (nested includes, links between libraries), not a count of files.

  • Method Details

    • hasMissing

      public static boolean hasMissing()
      Whether the running attempt has missed a resource, and will therefore be discarded: what it computes from now on is wasted. The includes, themes and libraries are all resolved while the diagram is parsed, so a rendering checks this after parsing and stops there (see PlantUMLBrowser.buildSvg); only Viz.js is asked for later, by the layout.

    • warn

      public static void warn(String message)
      Writes a warning to the console. During an attempt, it is held until the attempt is known to be the one that is kept, so that a discarded attempt does not repeat it.

    • requireViz

      public static void requireViz()
      Notes that the Viz.js instance is needed and not ready yet.
